title: Similarity, circles & quadratics
blurb: Same shape, circle facts, and the quadratic formula.

similar.name: Similar triangles
similar.phrase: Same angles, same shape. Every side grows by the same scale.
steps: Find the scale: big side ÷ matching small side.
Multiply any small side by the scale.
similar.exception: Similar is not the same as congruent. The sizes can be different. Always pair a side with the side across from the same angle.

bpt.name: Parallel cut in a triangle
bpt.phrase: A line parallel to the base cuts both sides in the same ratio.
steps: Read the two pieces on one side.
Set their ratio equal to the two pieces on the other side.
bpt.exception: Only if the cut is parallel to the base. A slanted line does not keep the ratio.

midseg.name: Midsegment
midseg.phrase: Join the middles: half the base, and parallel to it.
steps: Find the midpoint of two sides.
That line is half as long as the third side.
midseg.exception: Both ends must be midpoints. If one end is not the middle, the half rule does not apply.

semicircle.name: Angle in a semicircle
semicircle.phrase: A diameter always sees a right angle.
steps: Check that one side is a diameter.
The angle on the circle across from it is 90°.
The other two angles add to 90°.
semicircle.exception: The 90° is on the circle, not at the center. The center angle on a diameter is a straight line, 180°.

tangent.name: Tangent and radius
tangent.phrase: A tangent meets the radius at a right angle.
tangent.also: Two tangents from the same point are the same length.
steps: Draw the radius to the touching point.
Use the triangle angle sum for the rest.
tangent.exception: A line that cuts through the circle is not a tangent. A tangent only touches once.

quadratic.name: Quadratic formula
quadratic.phrase: Negative b, plus or minus the root of b² − 4ac, all over 2a.
steps: Read a, b, and c from ax² + bx + c = 0.
Use + and − to get both answers. Divide by 2a.
quadratic.exception: If a is 0, it is not a quadratic. If b² − 4ac is negative, there are no real answers. If it is 0, both answers are the same.

foil.name: FOIL expanding
steps: Add them and tidy like terms.
foil.exception: Watch the signs: (x − 3)(x + 2) still uses FOIL, but the insides and lasts pick up minuses. FOIL is for two brackets; three brackets need more steps.

dos.name: Difference of two squares
steps: Spot two squares with a minus between them.
Check by FOIL: the middle terms cancel.
dos.exception: It must be a minus. a² + b² does not factor over the reals this way. And 9x² − 4 is (3x − 2)(3x + 2), not (9x − 2)(x + 2).

factor.name: Factorising quadratics
factor.phrase: Find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b.
steps: For x² + bx + c, find two numbers with product c and sum b.
factor.exception: If the numbers you need do not exist as integers, it may not factor nicely. Leading coefficient not 1 needs a different hunt (or the quadratic formula).

ineq.name: Inequalities
ineq.phrase: Solve like an equation — but flip the sign when you × or ÷ by a negative.
steps: Move terms the same way you would for =.
If you multiply or divide both sides by a negative, flip < ↔ >.
ineq.exception: Adding or subtracting never flips the sign. Only multiplying or dividing by a negative does. Swapping sides also flips the inequality sign.

simul.name: Simultaneous equations
simul.phrase: Elimination: make one letter match, then add or subtract to wipe it out.
steps: Multiply so one letter has the same (or opposite) coefficient.
Add or subtract to eliminate that letter.
Solve for the other letter, then back-substitute.
simul.exception: If both letters wipe out and you get 0 = 5, there is no solution. If you get 0 = 0, there are infinitely many. Check by plugging both answers back in.

distmid.name: Distance and midpoint
distmid.phrase: Distance is Pythagoras on the grid. Midpoint averages the coordinates.
steps: Count the run and rise first if that feels easier.
distmid.exception: Do not add the coordinates for distance. Midpoint uses the average, not the difference.

perpgrad.name: Parallel and perpendicular slopes
perpgrad.phrase: Parallel: same slope. Perpendicular: flip the fraction and change the sign.
steps: Perpendicular: take the slope, flip it, and multiply by −1.
Check: m₁ × m₂ = −1 for perpendicular lines.
perpgrad.exception: Horizontal (slope 0) is perpendicular to vertical (undefined slope). A negative slope flipped stays careful with two minuses.

discr.name: Discriminant
discr.phrase: b² − 4ac tells how many real roots: positive two, zero one, negative none.
steps: From ax² + bx + c = 0, compute Δ = b² − 4ac.
discr.exception: The discriminant does not give the roots themselves — only how many. Complex roots exist when Δ < 0, but this lesson stays with real numbers.

scaleAV.name: Similar areas and volumes
scaleAV.phrase: Lengths × k, areas × k², volumes × k³.
steps: Find the length scale factor k.
If you are given areas, k = √(area scale).
scaleAV.exception: Do not scale area by k, or volume by k². A doubled length makes area ×4 and volume ×8.

bisector.name: Angle bisector theorem
bisector.phrase: The bisector cuts the opposite side in the ratio of the two adjacent sides.
steps: Confirm the ray bisects the angle.
Write adjacent side ÷ adjacent side = segment ÷ segment.
bisector.exception: It is the opposite side that is split. The ratio matches the two sides that form the angle, not the bisector length itself.

wordkeys9.name: Translate words to algebra
steps: Pick a variable for the unknown.
wordkeys9.exception: “Less than” reverses order: 3 less than x is x − 3, not 3 − x.

estimate9.name: Estimate irrational squares
estimate9.phrase: Squeeze between perfect squares to estimate √n.
estimate9.exception: √n is exact only for perfect squares.

commute9.name: Rearrange algebra
commute9.phrase: Terms can commute; factors can commute — keep signs glued to their terms.
steps: Write in a tidy order (often powers high to low).
commute9.exception: The minus sign belongs to the term that follows it when you commute.

distrib9.name: FOIL mindset
distrib9.phrase: FOIL: First, Outside, Inside, Last — then tidy.
distrib9.exception: FOIL is two binomials. More terms → use a grid.

compsupp9.name: Angle pairs in algebra
compsupp9.phrase: Complement → sum 90. Supplement → sum 180. Solve for x.
compsupp9.exception: Don’t assume adjacent — the problem must say complementary/supplementary (or show the figure).

zero9.name: Zero product property
zero9.phrase: If a product is zero, at least one factor is zero.
zero9.exception: Only works for zero on the other side. ab = 6 does not mean a=6.

complete9.name: Completing the square hook
complete9.phrase: Halve the middle, square it, park it on both sides.
steps: Square that half and add to both sides.
complete9.exception: Leading coefficient must be 1 (divide through first if not).

quadform9.name: Quadratic formula song
quadform9.phrase: x equals opposite b, plus or minus the square root of b squared minus 4ac, all over 2a.
quadform9.exception: If Δ < 0 there are no real roots. Don’t forget the “all over 2a” applies to everything.

prop9.name: Similar ratios
prop9.phrase: Same shape: matching sides stay in proportion — butterfly if needed.
prop9.exception: Correspondence matters — don’t match short to long casually.

exp9.name: Exponent mental moves
exp9.phrase: Multiply → add powers. Divide → subtract. Power of a power → multiply.
steps: Add/subtract/multiply the exponents as the law says.
exp9.exception: Different bases don’t combine with these laws (unless you rewrite).
